story: US jury convicts Huawei of fraud and trade secret theft in criminal trial
narration: Huawei has been convicted in New York on multiple federal criminal charges, including fraud, U.S. sanctions violations, and conspiracy to steal trade secrets. A federal jury found Huawei and three of its subsidiaries guilty of several offenses, such as bank and wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering. The trial, which lasted about three months, involved Huawei Technologies and its subsidiaries. These charges were first made public in 2019, shortly after the arrest of Huawei's Chief Financial Officer, Meng Wanzhou, in Canada. Sentencing for Huawei and its subsidiaries is scheduled for September 14, 2027.

story: China launches Shenzhou-24 mission to Tiangong space station with first foreign astronaut from Pakistan
narration: China launched the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft with a Pakistani astronaut on board, marking the first time a foreign national has flown to its Tiangong space station. The spacecraft lifted off at 8:18 am local time (0018 GMT) on 25 November 2026, a Wednesday morning, from the Jiuquan launch center in the Gobi Desert using a Long March-2F rocket. The crew includes Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi, and Pakistani pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first foreigner to fly on a Chinese crewed mission. The China Manned Space Agency described the launch as a "complete success" after the capsule separated from the rocket about ten minutes later and entered orbit. During the mission, the crew will conduct more than 90 scientific experiments and technology tests. Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, aged 40, is on a short-term mission and will return to Earth aboard Shenzhou-23 after completing an experiment involving photosynthetic cyanobacteria.

story: UK warns companies of potential Russian sabotage threat in unusual public announcement
narration: Britain’s Defence Ministry and MI5 have issued a warning to companies supporting Ukraine’s military, cautioning they may face sabotage attempts from Russia. The Ministry of Defence and the National Protective Security Authority stated that organisations involved in military procurement or supplying equipment to Ukraine could be targeted. The sabotage is said to involve proxy actors using low-sophistication methods such as arson. Russia’s embassy in London denied these claims, asserting that Russia has no plans or intentions to attack the UK. Last year, three British men were convicted for an arson attack on a warehouse storing Starlink satellite equipment bound for Ukraine, an act prosecutors linked to Russian military intelligence. The Ministry of Defence is holding closed-door security briefings with critical infrastructure and defence leaders, with Security Minister Dan Jarvis highlighting the seriousness of recent sabotage attempts across Europe.

story: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang returns to company, apologizes and vows improvement amid investigation
narration: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around. The AI hardware leader resigned from the company on Nov. 12 amid mounting scrutiny about alleged romantic relationships with subordinates and Alice Huang, a former executive at Singaporean cloud computing company Megaspeed. Less than a week later, Nvidia’s board announced that Huang would return to the company — backed by input from senior levels of the United States government that essentially guaranteed Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk. Huang reportedly apologized to Nvidia employees on Tuesday, the day after returning to the company as chief executive, saying he made terrible mistakes and is now in therapy for 90 minutes per day. The company's board reinstated Huang on Monday in a shock U-turn. Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's board, said Huang's return was in the best interests of stockholders, employees, partners, and customers. On Monday, former President Donald Trump said he spoke to the company's directors and convinced them to bring back Huang.

story: Australia’s inflation rate jumps to 4.9%, raising economic concerns
narration: Australia's inflation rate rose to 4.9% in the year to October, up from 4.3%, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics. The increase was driven by surging fuel costs, which climbed 6.3% in October and are about 33% higher over the year, and the end of electricity rebates, with prices 25% higher than a year ago. Building costs inflation also accelerated to 5.1%, while childcare, hairdressing, and insurance prices all rose by more than 5%. The Reserve Bank's preferred trimmed mean inflation measure increased to 3.8%, exceeding expectations. Despite this, the Reserve Bank of Australia is unlikely to raise interest rates at its December meeting. Economists anticipate inflation pressures will ease through 2027 as this year's shocks subside.

story: China-linked battery projects likely to receive UK funding despite security concerns
narration: A number of battery projects linked to China are set to receive UK state subsidies despite growing concerns about foreign interference risks to Europe's energy systems. Ofgem, Great Britain's energy regulator, published a provisional shortlist in June for a new long-duration energy storage scheme. Eleven projects using low-cost lithium-ion batteries, some backed by developers relying on Chinese manufacturers, made the 16-strong shortlist. One developer, Field Energy, sources batteries from Envision Energy, linked to the Chinese Communist Party. A UK government spokesperson said energy security remains a priority, with investments subject to strict national security scrutiny.

Dunleavy was last seen on the evening of January 9, 1968, leaving her job at a variety store in London, Ontario. She was found dead at a school 90 minutes later, with a head injury and strangulation as the cause of death. Moore, who was 25 at the time, had moved to Canada from Ireland in 1967.
